summary: The ledger rewrite lands once at the wave's end, so a wave outlasting many merges leaves a queue on disk listing entries already on the trunk

per.section: Fanout and worktrees — provisioning, isolation, teardown

acceptance: each shipped entry's ledger commit lands inside the same ship-lock hold as its own merge, so the queue on disk never lists an entry already on the trunk while a sibling's agent is still running, and a rewrite that refuses mid-wave carries its facts out through the holder the wave already takes a merge throw in
tests: a wave's first shipped entry leaves the queue on disk while a sibling's agent is still running
each shipped entry's ledger commit lands before the next entry's cherry-pick
